title: Taichung Arena Building Work Moves Ahead of Schedule
summaryZh: 台中巨蛋型體育館工程進度近兩成，超前預定，目標2030年完工。
summaryHi: ताइचुंग का नया इनडोर एरीना तय समय से आगे, लगभग 20% काम पूरा; 2030 तक तैयार होगा।
summaryEs: La construcción del nuevo pabellón de Taichung va adelantada: casi un 20 % hecho y fin previsto en 2030.
summaryJa: 台中の大型アリーナ建設が予定より早く進み、約2割完成。2030年完成を目指す。
summaryKo: 타이중 대형 실내 경기장 공사가 예정보다 빨라 약 20% 진행, 2030년 완공 목표.
summaryEn: Work on the Taichung Arena is nearly 20% done, ahead of plan, and should finish in 2030.
paragraphs: Construction of the Taichung Arena is running ahead of schedule, according to the Taichung City government, which said on Sunday that the project was close to 20% complete. The original timetable had expected just 15% by this point, and officials say the venue remains on course for completion in 2030.

Building work in Beitun District started on June 1, 2024, following years of planning. The city's Construction Bureau said excavation below ground had been completed and the project was now entering its main structural phase. Jointly designed by Japanese and Taiwanese architects, the complex covers roughly 6.95 hectares.

Once finished, the main arena will seat around 15,500 spectators and stage international competitions in sports such as basketball, volleyball, badminton, tennis and futsal, alongside concerts and large exhibitions. A secondary arena holding about 3,000 people will serve as a warm-up and training space and host smaller performances.

The design also places weight on sustainability, featuring rainwater recycling and energy-saving systems, as well as careful acoustic planning. An elevated open-air walkway with running paths will link the two halls, and a rooftop garden is planned.

Officials argue the arena will meet central Taiwan's long-standing demand for a major indoor venue. It is a separate project from the Taiwan Dome, a 45,000-seat baseball stadium for which the city signed a contract on Friday.
Taichung, a big city in central Taiwan, is building a new arena. An arena is a large building for sports and shows.
The city government said on Sunday that the work is almost 20% done. The plan was only 15% by now, so the work is ahead of time. It should finish in 2030.
Workers started in June 2024. They have finished digging under the ground. Now they are building the main parts.
The main hall will have about 15,500 seats. A smaller hall will have about 3,000 seats. People can watch basketball, volleyball, badminton and tennis there. There will also be concerts and shows.
The building will save water and energy. It will have a garden on the roof and paths for walking and running.

Work on the new Taichung Arena is moving faster than planned, the Taichung City government said on Sunday. The project in Beitun District is now nearly 20% complete, while the schedule expected only 15% at this stage. The city says it is on track to open in 2030.

Construction began in June 2024 after many years of planning. The underground work has now been finished, and builders are moving on to the main structure. The site covers about 6.95 hectares, and the arena was designed by Japanese and Taiwanese architects working together.

The main arena will have about 15,500 seats and will host international basketball, volleyball, badminton, tennis and martial arts events, as well as concerts and exhibitions. A second, smaller arena with about 3,000 seats will be used for training and smaller shows.
The design includes rainwater recycling and energy-saving features. A raised walkway will connect the two buildings, with paths for walking and running, and there will be a garden on the roof.
The city says central Taiwan needs a large indoor venue like those in the north and south. The arena is separate from the planned Taiwan Dome, a baseball stadium for at least 45,000 people.

Construction of the Taichung Arena is running ahead of schedule, according to the Taichung City government, which said on Sunday that the project was close to 20% complete. The original timetable had expected just 15% by this point, and officials say the venue remains on course for completion in 2030.

Building work in Beitun District started on June 1, 2024, following years of planning. The city's Construction Bureau said excavation below ground had been completed and the project was now entering its main structural phase. Jointly designed by Japanese and Taiwanese architects, the complex covers roughly 6.95 hectares.

Once finished, the main arena will seat around 15,500 spectators and stage international competitions in sports such as basketball, volleyball, badminton, tennis and futsal, alongside concerts and large exhibitions. A secondary arena holding about 3,000 people will serve as a warm-up and training space and host smaller performances.

The design also places weight on sustainability, featuring rainwater recycling and energy-saving systems, as well as careful acoustic planning. An elevated open-air walkway with running paths will link the two halls, and a rooftop garden is planned.

Officials argue the arena will meet central Taiwan's long-standing demand for a major indoor venue. It is a separate project from the Taiwan Dome, a 45,000-seat baseball stadium for which the city signed a contract on Friday.

The Taichung Arena, central Taiwan's long-awaited indoor sports and entertainment venue, is progressing faster than anticipated. City officials announced on Sunday that the project was nearly one-fifth complete, comfortably ahead of the 15% milestone set for this stage, and reaffirmed that it should be finished in 2030.

Ground was broken in Beitun District in June 2024 after a protracted planning period. According to the Construction Bureau, excavation for the four basement levels has been completed, allowing work to advance to the principal structure. The 6.95-hectare complex is the product of a collaboration between Japanese and Taiwanese architects.

Its main hall, with capacity for roughly 15,500 spectators, is intended to host international basketball, volleyball, badminton, tennis, futsal and martial arts events, as well as concerts and exhibitions. A 3,000-seat secondary hall will accommodate warm-ups, training sessions and more modest performances.

Environmental considerations feature prominently: the plans incorporate rainwater recycling, energy-efficient systems and dedicated acoustic design. The two halls will be connected by an elevated open-air walkway with jogging routes, complemented by a rooftop garden.

The city contends that the arena will fill a conspicuous gap, giving the centre of the island a venue comparable to those in the north and south. It should not be confused with the Taiwan Dome, a proposed 45,000-seat baseball stadium whose build-operate-transfer agreement was signed on Friday.

Taichung's flagship arena project appears to be defying the tendency of large public works to fall behind schedule. The city government reported on Sunday that construction had reached almost 20%, exceeding the 15% benchmark envisaged for this point, and that the venue was on track for completion in 2030.

Work in Beitun District commenced in June 2024 following extensive deliberation. With underground excavation now concluded, the Construction Bureau said the project was moving into its principal structural phase. The design, a joint undertaking by Japanese and Taiwanese architects, spans approximately 6.95 hectares.

The facility is designed to be versatile. Its main arena, accommodating some 15,500 spectators, will stage international tournaments in disciplines ranging from basketball and volleyball to martial arts, while also hosting concerts and exhibitions. An ancillary 3,000-seat hall will serve athletes' warm-up and training needs and smaller-scale events.

Sustainability is integral to the blueprint, which incorporates rainwater recycling, energy-saving technology and sophisticated acoustic engineering. An elevated walkway with running tracks will link the halls, supplemented by a rooftop garden intended as public green space.

Municipal officials maintain that the arena will remedy a longstanding regional imbalance, as central Taiwan has lacked a large indoor venue comparable to those in the north and south. The project is distinct from the planned Taiwan Dome, a 45,000-seat baseball stadium whose contract was finalised on Friday.

major.ex: The city is planning major road works.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

martial.en: relating to fighting; in "martial arts", sports like judo

meet.ex: The new cars meet strict safety rules.

milestone.en: an important stage or event in development

modest.ex: The town saw a modest rise in visitors.

moving.ex: They are moving the office to Cork.

municipal.en: of a city or town government

north.ex: We drove north for three hours.

open.en: to start a new place or service

people.ex: Many people visit the market on Sundays.

performances.en: shows of music, dance or theatre

period.ex: Prices rose during the holiday period.

phase.ex: The first phase of the project is complete.

places.ex: It is a great place to live.

plan.en: a set of ideas for doing something

planned.en: arranged to happen in the future

point.ex: This is the highest point in the city.

principal.ex: Rice is the principal food in the region.

prominently.en: in a way that is easily noticed

ranging.en: covering a range between two points

reached.en: got to a certain level or place

reaffirmed.en: stated again that something is true

remains.ex: Most visitors remain in the city centre.

remedy.ex: The school acted quickly to remedy the problem.

example.en: The council promised to remedy the problem quickly.
example.zh: 議會承諾會盡快解決這個問題。

note.meaning: （動詞）補救、糾正（問題或不良情況）。
note.usage: 後接問題名詞，如 remedy the situation / problem；比 fix 正式。名詞意為「補救辦法」。

noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने समस्या को जल्दी सुधारने का वादा किया।
noteHi.meaning: (क्रिया) किसी समस्या या गलत स्थिति को सुधारना।
noteHi.usage: remedy the situation/problem के रूप में; fix से अधिक औपचारिक। संज्ञा में अर्थ "उपाय"।

noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento prometió remediar el problema rápidamente.
noteEs.meaning: (Verbo) remediar, corregir un problema o una mala situación.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con remedy the situation/problem; más formal que fix. Como sustantivo significa "remedio".

noteJa.exampleTr: 議会はその問題を速やかに是正すると約束した。
noteJa.meaning: （動詞）問題や悪い状況を是正する、改善する。
noteJa.usage: remedy the situation / problem の形で使い、fix より改まった語。名詞では「救済策」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 의회는 그 문제를 신속히 바로잡겠다고 약속했다.
noteKo.usage: remedy the situation/problem 형태로 쓰며 fix보다 격식 있다. 명사로는 "해결책".

noteEn.meaning: To correct or fix a problem or bad situation.
noteEn.usage: More formal than "fix"; used with situation, problem or shortage.

reported.ex: Three cases were reported last week.

routes.en: ways from one place to another

running.en: the activity of moving fast on foot

say.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

schedule.en: a plan of when things will happen

seats.ex: All the seats on the bus were taken.

separate.ex: They did a separate test on the water.

serve.en: to provide a service to people

sessions.en: periods of time for an activity

sessions.ja: セッション；練習の時間

set.ex: No date has been set for the meeting.

should.en: used to say what is expected; (at the start) if

shows.ex: We saw two shows in London.

signed.en: wrote his name on an official paper

site.en: a place where something is built

sophisticated.ex: The car has a sophisticated computer system.

space.en: a room or area used for something

sports.ex: He likes all kinds of sports.

stadium.en: a large sports ground with seats

stage.en: a point or step in a process

sunday.ex: We visit my grandparents on Sunday.

taichung.en: a large city in central Taiwan

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

tendency.en: a likely way of behaving or happening

tennis.en: a sport played with rackets and a ball over a net

there.en: used to say something exists; that place

those.en: the ones there or already mentioned

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

timetable.en: a plan showing when things will happen

to.en: towards; also used before a verb

together.ex: Stir the eggs and milk together.

tournaments.ex: The city hosts two tennis tournaments a year.

track.zh: 軌道（on track 按計畫進行）
track.en: a path; "on track" means progressing as planned
track.ex: The project is on track to finish soon.

tracks.ex: The park has new running tracks.

training.ex: New staff get two weeks of training.

under.en: according to a rule or agreement

undertaking.ex: The landlord is undertaking to fix the roof.

venue.en: a place where an event happens

note.usage: 可形容人（多才多藝）或物（多功能）；常與 highly/extremely 連用。

noteEn.meaning: able to be used in many different ways.
noteEn.usage: Used for people and things; 'highly versatile'.

noteHi.exampleTr: बाँस एक बहुमुखी सामग्री है जो निर्माण और खाना पकाने में काम आती है।
noteHi.usage: लोगों और चीज़ों दोनों के लिए; highly versatile।

noteEs.exampleTr: El bambú es un material versátil para construir y cocinar.
noteEs.usage: Para personas u objetos; highly versatile.

noteJa.exampleTr: 竹は建築にも料理にも使える万能な素材だ。
noteJa.usage: 人にも物にも使う。highly versatile など。

noteKo.exampleTr: 대나무는 건축과 요리에 쓰이는 다용도 재료다.

volleyball.en: a sport where teams hit a ball over a high net
